knowledge:
- key_parameters: norm.method=Specifies the normalization method in normalize() (e.g., "quantile" for microarray/RNA-seq, "vst" for RNA-seq variance-stabilizing transformation) ;; de.method=Specifies the differential expression method in deAna() for RNA-seq (e.g., "edgeR", "DESeq2", "limma") ;; padj.method=Specifies the multiple testing correction method in deAna() (e.g., "BH") ;; method=Specifies the enrichment method in sbea() (e.g., "ora", "gsea", "safe", "padog", "roast", "camera", "gsva") or nbea() (e.g., "ggea", "spia", "pathnet") ;; org=Three-letter organism code (e.g., "hsa" for Homo sapiens) ;; db=Database for gene sets or networks (e.g., "kegg", "go", "msigdb", "enrichr") ;; perm=Number of permutations for significance estimation (set to 0 for classical hypergeometric test in ORA) ;; alpha=Significance level for filtering enriched gene sets ;; GROUP=A column name in colData defining the binary sample groups (1 for case, 0 for control) ;; BLOCK=A column name in colData defining paired samples or batch blocks
- alternatives: limma=Preferred for microarray differential expression ;; edgeR or DESeq2=Preferred for RNA-seq differential expression ;; ROAST or GSVA=Recommended for testing self-contained null hypotheses (directional association of genes in a set with phenotype) ;; PADOG or SAFE=Recommended for testing competitive null hypotheses (excess differential expression in a set relative to outside genes) ;; DAVID or GeneAnalytics=Preferred over enrichmentbrowser when analyzing simple gene lists without expression matrices
- when_to_use: Use when you have microarray or RNA-seq expression data and want to perform differential expression followed by set-based and/or network-based pathway enrichment analysis, and then combine and interactively browse the results.
- pitfalls: ORA (Overrepresentation Analysis) is prone to type I error rate inflation when genes are co-expressed within sets ;; GSEA, SAFE, and SAMGS require the full expression matrix for sample permutation and cannot be run on simple gene lists ;; Legacy enrichment methods (like GSEA and PADOG) applied to RNA-seq raw counts require a variance-stabilizing transformation (vst) or voom transformation first ;; Modifying package-wide configuration parameters via configEBrowser should be done with care to avoid impairing functionality.

workflows.name: microarray_enrichment_workflow
workflows.intent: Perform normalization, differential expression, set-based enrichment (ORA), network-based enrichment (GGEA), and combine results for microarray data.
workflows.stages: 1. Read expression data into a SummarizedExperiment ;; 2. Map probes to genes ;; 3. Normalize expression values ;; 4. Define sample groups ;; 5. Perform differential expression analysis ;; 6. Load gene sets ;; 7. Run set-based enrichment analysis (SBEA) ;; 8. Compile gene regulatory network ;; 9. Run network-based enrichment analysis (NBEA) ;; 10. Combine enrichment results ;; 11. Visualize and browse results
workflows.code:
library(EnrichmentBrowser)
data.dir <- system.file("extdata", package = "EnrichmentBrowser")
exprs.file <- file.path(data.dir, "exprs.tab")
cdat.file <- file.path(data.dir, "colData.tab")
rdat.file <- file.path(data.dir, "rowData.tab")
se <- readSE(exprs.file, cdat.file, rdat.file)
library(ALL) 
data(ALL)
ind.bs <- grep("^B", ALL$BT)
ind.mut <- which(ALL$mol.biol %in% c("BCR/ABL", "NEG"))
sset <- intersect(ind.bs, ind.mut)
all.eset <- ALL[, sset]
allSE <- probe2gene(all.eset)
allSE <- normalize(allSE, norm.method = "quantile")
allSE$GROUP <- ifelse(allSE$mol.biol =="BCR/ABL", 1, 0) 
allSE <- deAna(allSE, padj.method = "BH")
gmt.file <- file.path(data.dir, "hsa_kegg_gs.gmt")
hsa.gs <- getGenesets(gmt.file) 
sbea.res <- sbea(method = "ora", se = allSE, gs = hsa.gs, perm = 0, alpha = 0.1) 
gsRanking(sbea.res)
hsa.grn <- compileGRN(org="hsa", db="kegg")
nbea.res <- nbea(method="ggea", se=allSE, gs=hsa.gs, grn=hsa.grn) 
gsRanking(nbea.res)
res.list <- list(sbea.res, nbea.res) 
comb.res <- combResults(res.list)

workflows.name: rnaseq_enrichment_workflow
workflows.intent: Perform filtering, differential expression, ID mapping, variance-stabilizing transformation, and set-based enrichment (GSEA) for RNA-seq raw count data.
input: airway (SummarizedExperiment containing RNA-seq raw read counts and phenotype data)
workflows.stages: 1. Filter low-count genes ;; 2. Define sample groups and blocks ;; 3. Perform differential expression analysis using edgeR ;; 4. Map ENSEMBL gene IDs to NCBI Entrez IDs ;; 5. Apply variance-stabilizing transformation ;; 6. Run set-based enrichment analysis (GSEA)
workflows.code:
library(airway) 
data(airway)
airSE <- airway[grep("^ENSG", rownames(airway)),] 
airSE <- airSE[rowSums(assay(airSE)) > 4,]
airSE$GROUP <- ifelse(airway$dex == "trt", 1, 0)
airSE$BLOCK <- airway$cell 
airSE <- deAna(airSE, de.method = "edgeR")
airSE <- idMap(airSE, org ="hsa", from = "ENSEMBL", to = "ENTREZID") 
airSE <- normalize(airSE, norm.method = "vst")
air.res <- sbea(method = "gsea", se = airSE, gs = hsa.gs)
gsRanking(sbea.res)

workflows.name: all_in_one_pipeline
workflows.intent: Run the complete standardized enrichment analysis pipeline using the all-in-one wrapper function.
workflows.stages: 1. Execute the ebrowser wrapper function to run normalization, DE, SBEA, NBEA, and combine results
workflows.code: ebrowser( meth=c("ora", "ggea"), exprs=exprs.file, cdat=cdat.file, rdat=rdat.file, org="hsa", gs=hsa.gs, grn=hsa.grn, comb=TRUE, nr.show=5)
